first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and memory_31/memory_86 (clean, unflagged records) directly support that shortening/simplifying onboarding reliably lifts activation and completion in self-serve SMB accounts - addressing two of the three current problems with a single low-risk lever. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory explicitly flags a pooled-cohort readout after a mid-test redefinition, so its lift estimate is unreliable; racing on price also risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that erode long-term qualified revenue, contrary to the primary objective. I want to verify memory_73's original record to see if the effect holds in the uncorrupted cohort before ever committing scarce experiment capacity to it, and verify memory_31 to confirm the activation lift is durable and not confounded, since it's the basis for this week's action. Given only one experiment slot, I'm choosing the safer, better-evidenced onboarding fix over the unverified pricing response, and keeping scale modest (standard_experiment) rather than broad_rollout since we haven't yet re-tested at current conditions with competitor pressure in play.
